messages:
Ava Li: Quick kickoff Hi team I uploaded two variants for the Account settings form: Variant 1 = field-first error surfacing (helper text + red outline). Variant 2 = compact markers + contextual top banner that expands into a detail list. Also attached a draft for bulk destructive confirmations. Need quick takes on: clarity, density on small screens, and a11y implications. Jon Torres: skimmed them. My gut: field-first is fastest for single-field edits. Banner wins for multi-section saves. Mobile risk: expandable banner might get scrolled out of view. Priya N.: Agreed. Also: in dense lists inline text crowds the UI. For bulk failures we should show per-row status (icon + short message) and an overall banner when failures > 2. Ellen Park: Accessibility nits: banner must be announced and focusable. If we surface a banner on submit fail, move focus to it and use an assertive live region. e.g. ```
Save failed 1 errors. See details.
``` Ava Li: Good example. Copy question: current banner copy: "Save failed 3 problems need attention. Fix the highlighted fields or expand the list." Thoughts on tone/length? Jon Torres: Shorter = better: "Save failed 3 issues. See details below." We want something scannable and actionable. Also programmatically focus the first invalid field after the banner is announced. Priya N.: Required marker convo: prototypes use an asterisk only. Research shows asterisks aren't always noticed. Options: keep asterisk + small "Required" helper on desktops; mobile can hide the word but keep `aria-required`. I'm in favor of explicit "Required" on forms that affect billing or public names. Ellen Park: +1. Also add `aria-describedby` that ties input -> helper message when invalid. Ensure color isn't the only cue. Ava Li: For destructive flows we sketched: (A) modal with typed-confirm (type DELETE), (B) modal that requires exact-name entry, (C) non-blocking snackbar with undo. For irreversible org deletes I think we should prefer typed-confirm or exact-name. For bulk soft-deletes snackbar undo seems friendly. Jon Torres: Typed-confirm protects from mistakes but slows power users. Suggest rule: exact-name for org-level, typed-confirm for irreversible dataset/table deletes, snackbar undo for reversible bulk ops. Consider a short cooldown for repeated bulk deletes. Priya N.: Accessibility for typed-confirm: input must have clear label and instructions that a screen reader can announce. Also ensure keyboard focus lands in the input immediately and that the confirm button is reachable by keyboard. Add visible focus rings. LintBot: Auto-lint results: Variant 1 helper contrast = 3.7:1 (low). Variant 2 banner missing focus transfer on fail. Recommend helper text >= 4.5:1 and add programmatic focus to the banner using `element.focus()` after setting aria-live. Also add `aria-invalid` on invalid controls. Ellen Park: Actionable list: 1) raise inline helper contrast or use heavier weight; 2) add assertive aria-live banner + move focus to it on submit failure; 3) ensure first invalid field is focused after the banner; 4) show explicit "Required" label for critical fields (keep asterisk too); 5) reserve typed-confirm/exact-name for irreversible deletes; use snackbar undo for soft deletes. Ava Li: Great. I'll update the mocks with contrast adjustments, focus behavior, and copy options for exact-name wording. Will post new links here once PR is up. Tagging @Priya to draft exact-name phrasing. Thanks! :handshake:
